correctness.rationale: The maximum source-path length strictly increases on arcs and is automorphism-invariant, so quotient directed multigraph D/H remains acyclic and essential. Any arc-orbit path can be lifted by moving a representative arc with a group element to match the current lifted vertex; this preserves path presence and absence in full orbit selections. Hence constant barycentric coordinates on arc orbits give PL identifications |PF(D)|^H=|PF(D/H)| and similarly PM. The published Grinberg–Katthän–Lewis sphere theorem gives fixed dimensions |U/H|-2 and |E/H|-|U/H|-1. A g-invariant face contributes (-1)^(number of arc orbits -1) to augmented Lefschetz, so the orbit quotient's sphere Euler sign yields rank-one integral characters sgn(g|U) for PF, sgn(g|E)*sgn(g|U) for PM. This applies to each subgroup, including degree -1 boundary. Independent all-orbit-subset path-lifting and exact signed face calculations for S2×S2 on a 1-2-2-1 layered network recovered 8 PF/PM trace tests and all four subgroup orbits.
